_readme: ROADMAP 2.263 — the DISCLOSED, DATED exception list for react-hooks/rules-of-hooks.
The rule was enabled as ERROR on 2026-08-01. It had never been switched on, so a
codebase with ~1,900 hook call sites had zero enforcement of it, and two Model-tab
sections called hooks after an early return. Those two are FIXED in the same change.
WHY THE RULE EARNS 'error' — measured, not assumed. The 2.263 audit predicted those
two would THROW 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render.' Neither did.
On React 18.3.1, GoalSection logged a hooks-order warning and RECOVERED, and
OptionsSection was completely silent — no throw, no warning, correct render — because
zero hooks ran before its guard, leaving React an empty hook list to compare against.
A silent runtime is precisely why this belongs in lint: the rule is a CODE-INTEGRITY
guard against behaviour React does not define, not crash prevention. Nothing at
runtime would have told us either defect was there.
These 16 files were already violating the rule at tip d04c5a9b. They are NOT
excused — they are RECORDED, with exact counts, so that:
· a NEW violation in a file not listed here fails lint as an error;
· a violation ADDED to a listed file fails the ratchet (count went up);
· a violation FIXED in a listed file ALSO fails the ratchet, demanding the number
come down. An exception list that silently tolerates its own obsolescence is the
hand-maintained mirror this programme keeps getting bitten by.
scripts/ci/assert-rules-of-hooks-ratchet.mjs enforces all three directions, and
eslint.config.js BUILDS its override list from the 'files' key below — so the list
exists exactly once and the config and the ratchet cannot disagree.
198 of the 232 sit in two files (ReactFlowGraph 117, SandboxStreamPanel 81). Do not
fold their repair into an unrelated PR; it is its own piece of work. Rowed: ROADMAP 2.264.
2026-08-05, ROADMAP 2.474: BaselineToggleCard.tsx (2) LEFT THIS LIST BY DELETION, not by
repair — the component was unreachable dead code (its only mount was BaselineTargetRow,
which had zero mounts of its own) and both files were removed. The ratchet's CLEARED
branch fired on the deletion and demanded this edit, which is the mechanism working:
234 → 232, and the ceiling comes down with it so the two slots cannot silently re-open.
_maxTotal is the ENFORCED CEILING, not a comment: assert-rules-of-hooks-ratchet.mjs
fails if the per-file counts sum above it, and also fails if _total disagrees with
that sum. Lower it freely as violations are fixed. Raising it — or appending a file —
requires editing _maxTotal and _recordedOn in the same diff, so growth is a reviewed
decision rather than a quiet append.
